mainline_porting.note: Porting SailfishOS onto a mainline (non-hybris) kernel: what the ecosystem already provides and the traps met on the F(x)tec Pro1-X (qx1050, SM6115, Linux 7.1, SFOS 5.1.0.11) in October 2026. Labels: confirmed = observed on the device or read in the source; inferred.

method.research_first: confirmed (2026-10-23): every problem of the first bring-up day already had a worked solution in an existing port. Before implementing, send research agents at sailfish-on-dontbeevil (PinePhone: the only maintained mainline family), the hybris config of the same device, the sailfishos/* sources and the ngfd/mce/ofono trackers; then plan. Writing configs from scratch cost three blind fixes on vibration alone.
method.template_port: confirmed: sailfish-on-dontbeevil/droid-config-pinephone + piggz/droid-hal-configs branch native (droid-configs.inc with native_build 1) is the template for a mainline droid-config package: delete_file.list removes the hybris init bits, mic + a hand-maintained kickstart in a CI repo, rootfs tarball + flash script.
method.generated_not_shipped: confirmed: /etc/hw-release, /usr/lib/hw-release and the ssu board mapping are generated by droid-hal-version-<device> and droid-configs.inc; a bring-up tree may carry copies, a package must not.

vibration_ngfd.enospc: confirmed (sailfishos/ngfd src/plugins/ffmemless, kernel ff-memless.c): ngfd uploads one effect per name in supported_effects plus a default; the stock 50-ffmemless.ini lists 17 names (one is a typo, drag_boundary_drag_end), the kernel memless core has 16 slots, so on every plain FF_RUMBLE driver the 17th upload fails with ENOSPC, ngfd logs 'Could not load ngfd effects' and exits. Same report as ngfd PR #3 (PinePhone, 2021).
vibration_ngfd.fix: confirmed working: a file whose name ends in ffmemless.ini sorting after 50- (e.g. 60-<device>-ffmemless.ini) with [ffmemless] supported_effects = 12 names. Files with other names are NOT merged as plugin parameters; NGF_FFMEMLESS_SETTINGS only overrides parameters, not the list.
vibration_ngfd.qt_plugin: confirmed: qt5-feedback-haptics-ffmemless (priority Normal) bypasses ngfd and uploads 2-3 effects per process into the same 16 slots; HADK and the PinePhone pattern use libngf-qt5-qtfeedback instead.
vibration_ngfd.bus: confirmed: ngfd owns com.nokia.NonGraphicFeedback1.Backend on the SYSTEM bus; it registers only after its stream-restore/tonegen plugins reach PulseAudio. Test: gdbus call --system --dest com.nokia.NonGraphicFeedback1.Backend --object-path /com/nokia/NonGraphicFeedback1 --method com.nokia.NonGraphicFeedback1.Play feedback_press '@a{sv} {}' (event names from /usr/share/ngfd/events.d, not effect names).
vibration_ngfd.strength: confirmed: an FF_RUMBLE play that the kernel accepts can still be unfelt; module parameters of the motor driver (gain/drive) decide. Test the motor with a direct EVIOCSFF upload before blaming the stack.

audio_pulseaudio.stack: confirmed: PulseAudio 17 + UCM2 + pulseaudio-modules-nemo (parameters, mainvolume, stream-restore) + pulseaudio-policy-enforcement + ohm with policy-settings-common; arm_<device>_default.pa via /etc/sysconfig/pulseaudio CONFIG, xpolicy.conf with card/port names, x-maemo-*.table and /var/lib/nemo-pulseaudio-parameters from the droid-hal-configs template, /etc/ohm/*.ini and ohm-policy.conf (dbus policy) from the same template. The volume keys slider in lipstick needs module-dbus-protocol + mainvolume up before lipstick starts.
audio_pulseaudio.pa17_ucm_assert: confirmed: Jolla's pulseaudio 17.0+git1 aborts with Assertion 'dev == data->device' failed in pa_alsa_ucm_set_port() when two UCM verbs declare a device of the same name (the port object is shared per card). Upstream fix: ed3d4f08 'alsa-ucm: Replace port device UCM context assertion with an error' (2024-01). piggz's nemo:devel:hw:pine:dontbeevil ships pulseaudio 17.0+git2+master.20260702 with the fix; it installs on 5.1.0.11 and the Nemo modules keep working.
audio_pulseaudio.ucm_conflicts: confirmed: outputs sharing one PCM need ConflictingDevice lists, or PulseAudio builds combination ports.
audio_pulseaudio.kernel_build_matters: confirmed (2026-10-24): the same SFOS userspace was silent on some kernel builds and played on others from the same source, toolchain and DTB. A config bisect pointed at unrelated option groups (two disjoint halves both 'silent'), which is the signature of boot-time ordering, not semantics. Proof: on a silent kernel `rmmod snd_soc_sm8250; modprobe snd_soc_sm8250` (sound card re-created) made it play. Every ASoC state (PCM running, DSP back end, codec and amp widgets on, amp enable GPIOs high) looks identical in both cases, so the state dumps cannot tell. Workaround: re-register the card once before the user session (qx1050-audio-reprobe.service). Kernel root cause (which component the first card probe races: codec clock, soundwire enumeration, ADSP service) still open.
audio_pulseaudio.ears_free_test: confirmed: tools/audio-loopback-test.sh records the built-in mic (hw:0,1 via UCM Mic) while speaker-test plays 440 Hz on hw:0,0 and compares RMS (od -td2 | awk); noise floor ~220 on the Pro1-X. Needs one calibration on a playing kernel. Lets the bisect/reboot loop run without a listener.
audio_pulseaudio.mem_4g_test: confirmed: booting a silent kernel with mem=4G did not help; the q6asm DAI device sits in an IOMMU DMA domain (apps_smmu 0x1c1, group type DMA), so the DSP gets IOVAs, not physical addresses.
audio_pulseaudio.policy_notify_loop: On a mainline port with ALSA UCM, every route (earpiece, speaker, headset) is its own PulseAudio card profile, so a profile switch removes the sink and creates a new one. SailfishOS's policy module (module-policy-enforcement, xpolicy.conf) reports device availability to ohmd for every [device] rule without disable_notify. The sink removal is reported as 'all built-in devices gone' (com.nokia.policy info '0'), ohmd reroutes, the new sink is reported back ('1'), ohmd reroutes again: a profile ping-pong. Android-based ports never see it because the droid card has one profile and routes by port only. Give every [device] rule that matches the built-in card's sink the disable_notify flag. Pro1-X 5.2.0.22, 2026-10-28, port commit f4f1bef.
audio_pulseaudio.call_volume_keys: The volume keys during a call move module-meego-mainvolume's virtual call stream (a PulseAudio sink input with driver module-meego-mainvolume), not the sink. On a mainline port whose call audio bypasses PulseAudio (q6voice in the DSP), follow that stream's volume and apply it to a codec or DSP gain. Pro1-X 5.2.0.22, 2026-10-29, qx1050-voicecall 0.1-6 (port commit 9f784e6).
audio_pulseaudio.call_test_streams: In a voice-call card profile the audio policy routes untagged test streams to the null sink, and an untagged recording aborted PulseAudio 17 (pa_channels_valid). Tag test streams into the call group (xpolicy.conf property). Pro1-X, 2026-10-29.
audio_pulseaudio.lipstick_waits_on_ofono: A hung ofono (started on a modem that was not prepared, e.g. after a modem crash during boot) keeps lipstick on a spinner before the lock screen: lipstick's D-Bus calls to ofono time out one after another. Start ofono only once the modem is ready and restart it after a modem restart. Pro1-X 5.2.0.22, 2026-10-29 (port commit 7533a36).
audio_pulseaudio.notification_led_multicolor: mce-plugin-libhybris has no backend for a kernel multicolor LED (one rgb:status device). Pro1-X adds a 'multicolor' backend (port patches/mce-plugin-libhybris, commit 53d590a) selected by [LEDConfigHybris] BackEnd=multicolor, LedDirectory=/sys/class/leds/rgb:status. mce's default pattern colors: calls green, SMS/IM blue, email yellow, notifications cyan, battery full white.
audio_pulseaudio.charging_notification_order: lipstick's BatteryNotifier shows 'Charging' (with sound) when mce's charger_state is on, the battery is not full and the usb-moded target mode is undefined/ask/charging/charger, evaluated 100 ms after the last change. mce's charger_state is on while any charger is online OR the battery reports Charging, and mce coalesces udev events in 50 ms windows. On a mainline port usb-moded can pick a mode within 50 ms of the plug (charging notification suppressed: none on plug-in) and the battery's Discharging can come after usb-moded's 'undefined' on unplug (notification and sound on the unplug). Fixes: usb-moded -m <ms> cable connection delay via USB_MODED_HW_ADAPTATION_ARGS in /var/lib/environment/usb-moded/*.conf (hybris gets the delay from Android gadget enumeration; an XA2 runs without -m), and a battery driver that reports Discharging before the charger supply's offline event. Pro1-X 5.2.0.22, 2026-10-29, port commit d5693f7. Diagnose with dbus-monitor on com.meego.usb_moded and com.nokia.mce.signal plus udevadm monitor --kernel.
audio_pulseaudio.low_power_mode_display: mce's low power mode (mcetool -E enabled; --blank-screen-lpm only from a lit display; LPM UI triggering default from-pocket; blank-from-lpm-on timeout) works on a mainline port with lipstick's LPM view: on the Pro1-X it showed the LPM clock for the timeout after the display blanked, then black; not after a power-key blank. It is a short 'glance' view, not an always-on display: with a video-mode DSI panel the SoC must keep feeding frames, so a permanent display prevents suspend. An AOD would need panel self-refresh/command mode. Evaluated and switched off again by moWerk, 2026-10-30.

mce.keyboard_backlight: confirmed (mce 1.116.5): 'Keyboard backlight: disabled' in mcetool is the LED's current state, not a setting; [KeyPad] BrightnessDirectory points at the LED dir; it turns on with slide open + display on. The 1.119 keypad rewrite (BinaryBrightnessFile, dconf enable) is not in SFOS 5.1.
mce.slide_switch: confirmed: [SW_KEYPAD_SLIDE] keys are the keyboard's evdev NAME ('Pro1X keyboard', 'Keyboard extra keys' on mainline) mapped to the switch device name; a wrong name only breaks keyboard_available (VKB hiding), the slide itself still blanks/unblanks.
mce.backlight_write_einval: confirmed: mce writes to a DCS panel backlight after blanking return EINVAL ('can't flush .../brightness'); harmless log noise. The visible flash at every blank on the BOE bf060y8m panel was a different bug: display off sent from the panel's unprepare after the video stream stopped (one corrupted full-brightness frame); fixed by sending it from .disable (Pro1-X kernel patch 0023, 2026-10-29).

modem_ofono.qrtr: confirmed: Jolla's ofono 1.29 fork has no QRTR support (qmimodem disabled, gobi plugin is USB QMUX only). Upstream ofono >= 2.9 has plugins/qrtrqmi.c; the PinePhone port runs upstream ofono 2.12 under SFOS 5.x; sailfishos-native/ofono carries 2.13 + the slot manager patches, but nobody wired qrtrqmi into the slot manager (~270 lines, gobi slot shim as template). ModemManager has no consumer on SFOS.
modem_ofono.uim_provisioning: confirmed: on this modem firmware the primary GW provisioning session must be activated once (qmicli --uim-change-provisioning-session with the USIM AID); postmarketOS does it every boot with msm-modem-uim-selection (idempotent).
modem_ofono.udevng_needs: confirmed (ofono plugins/udevng.c): the qrtrsoc modem needs rmnet_ipa0 plus three rmnet_dataN links created beforehand.
modem_ofono.sim_cards_settings_page: The Settings > SIM cards page is the package jolla-settings-networking-multisim, pulled in only by multi-SIM device configuration patterns (C2: patterns-sailfish-device-configuration-s19mps). A port on patterns-sailfish-device-configuration-common lacks it: install it explicitly (Pro1-X 5.2.0.22, 2026-10-27, port commit 6ac21e8).

sensors_camera.ssc: confirmed: SM6115 sensors live on the ADSP (SSC); NixOS uses hexagonrpcd (PR27 fork) + iio-sensor-proxy with libssc. sensorfw has no adaptor for that and net.hadess.SensorProxy exposes no raw accel/gyro, so a sensorfw adaptor linking libssc is the only path (weeks).
sensors_camera.camera: confirmed: native-common OBS has libcamera 0.4.0 with libgstlibcamera; jolla-camera's camerabin takes QT_GSTREAMER_CAMERABIN_VIDEOSRC=libcamerasrc; piggz's Shutter is the proven fallback app.
sensors_camera.qtsensors_sensors_conf: QtSensors' sensorfw plugin registers its backends only from the [Default] section of /etc/xdg/QtProject/Sensors.conf (QAccelerometer=sensorfw.accelerometer and so on). Hybris ports get it from droid-hal-configs; a mainline port that does not use droid-hal-configs must ship it, or every app and lipstick logs 'Could not connect to the <type> sensor backend' and never asks sensorfwd for a sensor, while sensorfwd itself works. Pro1-X SailfishOS 5.2.0.22: Dodger got null readings, lipstick no orientation; sensorfwd at --log-level=debug showed the SSC adaptor delivering samples and a sensortestapp client receiving them. Copying droid-hal-configs sparse/etc/xdg/QtProject/Sensors.conf fixed apps and auto-rotation (port commit fee23c2).
sensors_camera.sensorfw_hw_settings_features: sensorfwd's [available] section (20-sensors-default.conf) maps sensors to ssu-sysinfo hardware features (Feature_AccelerationSensor, Feature_ProximitySensor, ...), read from /usr/share/csd/settings.d/hw-settings.ini [features]. Without that file only Suspend and Reboot exist and every sensor is 'plugin not available'. The same list gates Settings items (auto brightness needs FeatureLightSensor) and the status-bar battery indicator. Pro1-X 5.2.0.22: adding hw-settings.ini (port commit 8b6f01d) made sensorfw load all sensors; the battery indicator in the home screen bar appeared at the same time.
sensors_camera.settings_pages_from_device_patterns: Jolla's per-device and consumer patterns, not the common one, pull several Settings packages: jolla-settings-networking-multisim (SIM cards), jolla-settings-system-orientation (Display > Orientation, the top-menu orientation lock, 'Rotating homescreen'), jolla-settings-system-sideloading. A port on patterns-sailfish-device-configuration-common must list them. jolla-settings-system-flashlight is only the toggle QML; it requires a virtual sailfish-flashlight-provider (session D-Bus service org.sailfish.flashlight.provider: toggleFlashlight -> b, property flashlightOn, signal flashlightOnChanged(b)). On hybris that is droidmedia-flashlight (sailfishos/droidmedia flashlight/, Apache-2.0, Qt + libresourceqt RearFlashlightType, D-Bus activated, quits after 2 min idle). A native port provides it with a sysfs LED backend: Pro1-X sysfs-flashlight (port commit 43073d5), LED brightness files made writable for the video group by udev. Pro1-X 5.2.0.22, 2026-10-28, port commits 6ac21e8 and a2e16ce.
sensors_camera.ssc_reports_in_phone_frame: libssc readings from the Qualcomm Sensor Core are already rotated into the device frame by the SSC registry; a mount matrix taken from an IIO-based stack (iio-sensor-proxy ACCEL_MOUNT_MATRIX) can invert axes. Start from identity and verify by tilting (a tilt game, auto-rotation). Pro1-X: the NixOS matrix -1,0,0,0,-1,0,0,0,1 inverted X (Dodger) and Y (Horizon) and turned auto-rotation upside down; identity in sensorfw's transformation_matrix (port commit 75609c2). Sensor chips per SSC attributes: lsm6ds3c accel/gyro, mmc56x3x magnetometer, TXC PA22A light/proximity (on-change).

dual_boot_nixos.layout: confirmed: SFOS rootfs as a directory on the NixOS ext4, busybox initramfs bind-mounting it (keep the parent fs at /mnt/nixos; a second mount of the device is refused once the bind shows it on /), U-Boot extlinux one-shot entry restored by the initramfs.
dual_boot_nixos.nixos_wifi: confirmed: NixOS's Wi-Fi MAC is random per connection; find the phone by ssh host key scan. SFOS: udev rule derives a stable MAC from machine-id so connman remembers the network.
dual_boot_nixos.bluetooth_repower: confirmed: wcn399x on hci_uart_qca works when enabled from boot; after a power-down it never answers again (0xfc00 tx timeout), unbind shows a regulator refcount WARNING. Kernel item.

camera_jolla_camera.stack: confirmed (Pro1-X, 2026-10-25): jolla-camera on mainline = Sailfish qtmultimedia camerabin with QT_GSTREAMER_CAMERABIN_VIDEOSRC=libcamerasrc inside wrappercamerabinsrc; needs qtmultimedia patches for libcamera enumeration (libcameraprovider, camera-name), size-less source caps, late-frame drop, initial ready-for-capture, sizes from the device provider (port/patches/qtmultimedia 0001-0007 in the Pro1-X port).
camera_jolla_camera.sandbox: confirmed: sailjail hides /usr/share/libcamera, the software ISP then fails and the viewfinder is black; whitelist it in /etc/firejail/disable-common.local. Files pushed to the device must be root-owned or firejail fcopy aborts every sandboxed app.
camera_jolla_camera.video_encoders: confirmed: jolla-camera records MP4 (video/quicktime variant=iso) with video/x-h264 and audio/mpeg mpegversion=4; on hybris both come from droidmedia. Native: AAC = gst-libav avenc_aac, registered with rank none, so set GST_PLUGIN_FEATURE_RANK=avenc_aac:primary in the session env; H.264 = the SoC's V4L2 stateful encoder via v4l2h264enc. Without encoders the app writes 965-byte empty MP4s and gst.log says 'Couldn't create encoder for format video/x-h264'.
camera_jolla_camera.gst_v4l2_probe: confirmed: Jolla builds gstreamer1.0-plugins-good with -Dv4l2-probe=false, which compiles out v4l2h264enc/v4l2h264dec registration even when /dev/videoN is a working encoder. Rebuild the package with v4l2-probe=true (Version 1.26.11+git1, Release above 1.14.2.jolla).
camera_jolla_camera.venus_sm6115: confirmed: SM6115/QCM2290 Venus (AR50LT) binds the gen1 venus driver via the qcom,qcm2290-venus fallback (Linux 7.1 + the 2026 sm6115 venus DT node). The driver requires firmware >= 6.0.55 (encoder needs secure buffers below 6.0.54); the Pro1-X vendor image is 6.0.49 and fails with -EINVAL. linux-firmware qcom/venus-6.0/venus.mbn (6.0-00055) loads on the Pro1-X. Result: 1080p30 H.264 in hardware, about 30 fps including a CPU videoconvert to NV12.
camera_jolla_camera.video_size: confirmed: jolla-camera picks the largest size of the chosen aspect ratio; per-mode videoResolution keys are ignored. /apps/jolla-camera/maxVideoResolution='WxH' (dconf, read in cameraconfigs.cpp) caps it, e.g. 1920x1080 for a 1080p encoder.
camera_jolla_camera.orientation: confirmed: libcamera's Rotation property equals QCameraInfo::orientation (Qt: sensor top at screen right = 270; Android: 90; libcamera's Android HAL uses 360 - Rotation). jolla-camera does not rotate its VideoOutput; the hybris video texture backend rotates by droidcamsrc's image-orientation tag. With Qt's default renderer the viewfinder is unrotated unless qtmultimedia adds the camera orientation (Pro1-X port patch 0007; not yet verified in the app as of 2026-10-25 03:00).

own_kernel_tree.why: confirmed (moWerk 2026-10-26): leave NixOS behind; the port gets its own clean mainline base, camera and sensors are fixed on it rather than on 7.1 and then rebased.
own_kernel_tree.base_finding: confirmed: the community branch the NixOS flake used (sm6115-mainline/linux qx1050-7.1) is plain v7.1, its tip is Linus's 'Linux 7.1' commit. All device support was in the flake's patch files, so an own kernel is mainline plus that series, nothing else to extract.
own_kernel_tree.rebase_7_1_to_7_3: confirmed: of 12 device patches and 4 SFOS patches, 9+3 applied with offsets only; the pinctrl egpio patch and the venus SoC node + gcc flag were upstream by 7.3. Every reject was in the board DTS: upstream changed two lines there (touch irq-gpios flag, Type-C vbus-supply). Method that worked: apply each patch's DTS hunks to the 7.1 file in sequence and 3-way merge each step onto the 7.3 file (git merge-file); one conflict, resolved to ours.
own_kernel_tree.pitfall_patch_N: confirmed: patch -N skips a hunk it sees as reversed but applies the rest of the same patch; with the venus node already upstream it added a second copy of the node at a new offset. Check every 'Reversed' patch for duplicates.
own_kernel_tree.pitfall_iio_namespace: confirmed: since 7.2 the IIO consumer API is exported in the IIO_CONSUMER namespace; an out-of-tree driver using it fails modpost until MODULE_IMPORT_NS("IIO_CONSUMER").
own_kernel_tree.pitfall_nix_config: confirmed: the Nix kernel config (manualConfig) is never resolved by Kconfig, so it can claim values Kconfig would refuse (BT_RFCOMM=y with BT=m). A plain defconfig + fragment + olddefconfig build exposes them; check every fragment line after olddefconfig.
own_kernel_tree.config_renames_7_3: confirmed: PROC_SYSCTL is gone as an option (proc_sysctl builds with SYSCTL); CRYPTO_DEV_QCE depends on BROKEN; the Qualcomm RNG is HW_RANDOM_QCOM.
own_kernel_tree.build_without_nix: confirmed: rootless podman, Debian trixie with gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu plus host gcc/libc6-dev (fixdep is a host tool), defconfig + fragments, Image + dtb + modules_install, about 20 minutes at 12 threads on a Ryzen 5850U.

usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.usb-moded on a mainline kernel: configfs: A precomposed legacy gadget built into the kernel (g_cdc, g_ether) owns the UDC, so usb-moded cannot run and Settings offers only 'charging only'; no plug notification either (mce takes the cable state from usb-moded). Build the legacy gadget as a module and CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS=y; create the configfs gadget before usb-moded starts (on hybris Android's init does it): gadget g1, configs/b.1, functions rndis.usb0 and ffs.mtp, FunctionFS mounted at /dev/mtp; name the functions in [configfs] (function_rndis, function_mtp). usb-moded detects the cable through /sys/class/power_supply/usb (online, type USB / USB_DCP / USB_CDP); a Type-C tcpm source supply does not show a PC host as online. Developer mode configures interface rndis0: set the RNDIS function's ifname to 'rndis%d' right after mkdir, before the first bind (later writes do not rename). Pro1-X 7.3 SailfishOS 5.2.0.22: plug notification and sound, developer mode 192.168.2.15 (host got .5), MTP visible as 2931:0a07 'Jolla Oy Phone MTP'. usb-moded-mtp-mode-android-ffs supplies the ffs MTP mode.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.mce charge limit needs only an on/off co: SailfishOS implements the charge limit in mce (Settings > Battery appears when mce has a charging control): it writes enable/disable values to a control file at its thresholds; it probes battery_charging_enabled, charging_enabled and input_suspend under /sys/class/power_supply/battery, or [Charging] ControlPath/EnableValue/DisableValue in its config. mce looks for the file once at start: if the driver providing it loads later, the limit silently disappears; order mce after it (ExecStartPre wait). Kernel side: a writable attribute toggling the charger's charge-enable bit; disabling charging (not the input) keeps the phone powered from USB. Pro1-X: PMI632 CHGR_ENABLE_CMD 0x1042 bit 0 as charging_enabled on the pro1x-charger-icl device (patch 0017); the vendor kernel on the hybris port offers input_suspend. Verified: charging stops at the set 80 % (current ~0 mA, status Not charging after patch 0020).
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Keep the user session independent of slo: systemd-user-sessions orders after network.target; ofono is WantedBy network.target and a modem-preparation unit ordered before ofono therefore delays the whole UI until the modem is ready (here up to a minute, the modem restarts once at boot). Mask network.target.wants/ofono.service in /etc and let the preparation unit (Type=simple) start ofono when done. For a late Wi-Fi interface that needs a stable MAC before connman files networks, do not hold connman (that again delays the session): set the MAC from a udev-started unit and restart connman once. On SailfishOS systemctl is /usr/bin/systemctl (not /bin). Pro1-X: user@100000 at 14.4 s instead of 56.8 s; Wi-Fi reconnects with the saved network under the stable identity.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.libssc blocks its caller's main loop whi: libssc 0.4.4 waits for the SSC 'registry' sensor with g_usleep(1 s) inside the report callback, up to 100 times, and counts other clients' discovery replies as failed polls. In sensorfwd this freezes the event loop: clients (lipstick's orientation sensor) stall, lipstick took 25 s to start instead of 7 s. Fix: ignore non-'registry' replies while waiting, retry from g_timeout_add_seconds. And start hexagonrpcd at boot, or the service never appears. Pro1-X: patch 0002 in port packages/libssc (0.4.4-2); lipstick restart 25.1 s -> 7.0 s; hexagonrpcd enabled at boot 2026-10-28.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Speaker amplifier pops: switch it on aft: An external speaker amplifier modelled as a PGA with PRE_PMU/POST_PMD events is powered while the codec's DAC and output drivers power up and down, and amplifies their transients: a loud pop at every card power cycle (boot, notification sounds, idle suspend, even plugging USB when that plays a sound). Model it as a speaker widget (SND_SOC_DAPM_SPK: powered up last, down first, POST_PMU/PRE_PMD) and give it a few ms after its power-down command before dropping the enable line. Pro1-X AW87339 x2 behind WCD9370 HPH outputs (kernel patch 0019): power-up pop gone; a pop at card teardown during the boot-time card re-registration remains.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Give the charger a usb power supply and: Userspace (usb-moded, mce, UIs) expects /sys/class/power_supply/usb with online and type. A board charger driver that only manages the input current should still register it; with supplied_to the battery driver gets external_power_changed and can update its status at once instead of at its next poll. Report Not charging when input is present but no current flows (charge limit). Pro1-X pro1x-charger-icl/pro1x-adc-battery (patches 0018, 0020): unplug reflected within about a second instead of up to 5-10 s.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Check that the GPU votes for memory band: An Adreno GPU node without an interconnects path and without opp-peak-kBps in its OPPs never votes DDR bandwidth: the GPU clocks up to its top OPP but DDR stays at whatever CPU and display request, and bandwidth-bound rendering (overdraw, large textures, many layers) is slow and erratic. Check /sys/kernel/debug/interconnect/interconnect_summary under load (the GPU master, e.g. qnm_gpu, must show a peak vote). Copy the pattern from a sibling SoC upstream (MASTER_GFX3D/GRAPHICS_3D -> SLAVE_EBI, per-OPP peak bandwidth). Measure with a fixed-load benchmark, 3 runs each, fresh boot for both sides: the first run of a starved GPU can look fine before it drops. Pro1-X SM6115 Adreno 610, kernel 7.3, Mesa 25.1.8 freedreno, 2026-10-28: qnm_gpu 0/0 before; agatti (QCM2290) values 1.72/2.93/3.88/6.88 GB/s added (port kernel patch 0021). Benchymark: Benchy large +25 % and stable, Overdraw +37 %, Shader light +8 %, Icon storm +6 %, Shader heavy unchanged. GPU frequency was not the limit (devfreq at 950 MHz in both).
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Power-off alarm works on mainline: Pro1-X 5.2/7.3, 2026-10-28: Clock alarm, phone powered off and unplugged, it switched itself on and rang 55 s into the boot. dsme programs the PMIC RTC relative to its own (1970) clock; Linux cannot set the RTC (TrustZone, EPERM; dsme logs 'IPHB: could not set rtc time', harmless). Test only with a real alarm and unplugged.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Modem watchdog crash at boot (unsolved): About every second boot the modem stalls before requesting its EFS from rmtfs and the watchdog restarts it after 40 s; Wi-Fi, data and SIM come up a minute late. Ruled out: rmtfs order, PD mapper, IPA, early start, SIM polling alone. Port notes/modem-dog-crash.md.
usb_charging_boot_2026_10_28.Mic loopback as audio oracle: audio-loopback-test.sh (tone through the speaker, RMS on the mic) gives PLAYS/SILENT without ears; showed the sound card re-registration workaround is still needed on 7.3.

mainline_porting.system_sleep: CONFIRMED (2026-10-30, Pro1-X mainline 7.3): mce suspends through /sys/power/autosleep; a kernel without CONFIG_PM_AUTOSLEEP never suspends (suspend_stats success 0 after hours with the screen off). SM6115 offers s2idle only. The first manual s2idle resume crashed the ADSP sensor process (fastrpc resend of the frozen hexagonrpcd call); the TB-J606L port's fastrpc and SMP2P sleepstate patches are the fix (see Mainline/firmware_remoteproc). Wi-Fi deauthenticates before sleep and reconnects about 5 s after resume (no WoWLAN).
